title: Service Contract for the Maintenance of Production Equipment

content.text: Service Contract for the Maintenance of Production Equipment
Contract number:
Effective date:
[DATE_1].
Parties
This service contract is entered into between [ORG_1], [ADDRESS_1], represented by its managing director [PERSON_1] (hereinafter the
"Customer"
), and [ORG_2], [ADDRESS_2], represented by its managing director [PERSON_2] (hereinafter the
"Contractor"
). The Customer and the Contractor are hereinafter referred to individually as a "Party" and jointly as the "Parties".
Preamble

The Customer operates a metal-processing plant with approximately 600 employees, in which sheet metal parts, welded assemblies and machined components are produced for the commercial vehicle and agricultural machinery industries. Production takes place in two shifts from Monday to Friday and, depending on order volume, in a third shift and on Saturdays. The availability of the production equipment is therefore of central importance for the Customer's delivery reliability.

The Contractor is a specialist company for the maintenance and repair of machine tools, presses and industrial handling equipment. It employs qualified service technicians and maintains a regional service base within a driving distance of 60 minutes from the Customer's plant. The Parties wish to set out in this contract the terms on which the Contractor will maintain the Customer's production equipment.
1. Subject Matter of the Contract

1.1 The Contractor undertakes to carry out the preventive maintenance, inspection and corrective maintenance of the production equipment listed in Annex 1 (hereinafter the "Equipment") in accordance with the provisions of this contract. Annex 1 lists each item of Equipment with its manufacturer designation, year of construction, serial number and location in the plant.

1.2 The services under this contract are services within the meaning of Sections 611 et seq. of the German Civil Code (BGB), unless a specific service is expressly agreed as a work performance. Repairs carried out under clause 2.2 are subject to the provisions on contracts for work (Sections 631 et seq. BGB) with regard to the result of the repair.

1.3 The Equipment list in Annex 1 may be amended by mutual agreement in text form. New machines are included in the contract from the first day of the month following their acceptance by the Customer. The monthly flat fee is adjusted in accordance with the price list in Annex 3.
1.4 Not included in the scope of this contract are:
the maintenance of buildings, building services, compressed air generation and the central extraction system
the repair of damage caused by improper operation, external influences or force majeure
modifications, upgrades or retrofits of the Equipment, unless commissioned separately
software updates of machine controls that go beyond the installation of security updates provided by the manufacturer
2. Scope of Maintenance Services

The Contractor shall perform all services with the care of a prudent specialist company and in accordance with the recognised rules of technology, the operating instructions of the Equipment manufacturers and the applicable occupational health and safety regulations. The Contractor shall only use technicians who have the necessary qualifications and who have been instructed in the Customer's plant regulations.
2.1 Preventive Maintenance

The Contractor shall carry out preventive maintenance of the Equipment at the intervals specified in the following table. The intervals are based on the manufacturers' recommendations and on the Customer's operating conditions, in particular the two-shift operation and the high proportion of stainless steel processing.
Equipment
Maintenance task
Interval
Laser cutting systems (3 units)
Cleaning and adjustment of the beam guidance, inspection of the cutting head, filter change
Monthly
CNC press brakes (5 units)
Inspection of the hydraulic system, oil analysis, check of the safety light curtains
Quarterly
Eccentric presses (2 units)
Inspection of the clutch and brake, measurement of the stopping time
Quarterly
Robotic welding cells (4 units)
Calibration of the robot axes, inspection of the wire feed and torch cleaning station
Quarterly
CNC machining centres (6 units)
Spindle analysis, lubrication, geometry check, coolant inspection
Semi-annually
Overhead cranes (8 units)
Statutory inspection according to accident prevention regulations
Annually
Powder coating line
Inspection of the conveyor, the spray booths and the curing oven
Semi-annually
Industrial trucks and lifting equipment (12 units)
Statutory inspection and inspection of the load-bearing equipment
Annually

The Contractor shall propose a maintenance schedule for the following calendar year to the Customer by 31 October of each year. The schedule shall take into account the Customer's production planning, the plant shutdown periods in summer and at the turn of the year, and the availability of the Customer's maintenance staff. The Customer shall approve the schedule or request changes within two weeks.

Preventive maintenance work shall generally be carried out during the Customer's normal working hours from Monday to Friday between 6:00 and 22:00. Work requiring a longer stoppage of the Equipment shall be scheduled in the plant shutdown periods or on Saturdays, provided the Customer agrees.

After each maintenance visit, the Contractor shall prepare a service report documenting the work performed, the measured values, the replaced parts and any defects found. The report shall be uploaded to the Customer's maintenance portal within three working days. Defects that may affect the safety of the Equipment shall be reported to the Customer's maintenance manager immediately and verbally before the technician leaves the site.
2.2 Corrective Maintenance

In the event of a malfunction or breakdown of the Equipment, the Contractor shall carry out the necessary repairs within the response and restoration times set out in clause 3. The Customer shall report malfunctions via the Contractor's service hotline or service portal, stating the affected Equipment, a description of the fault and the priority level.

The Contractor shall first attempt to rectify the fault by remote diagnosis, provided the Equipment concerned allows remote access and the Customer has approved such access in the specific case. If the fault cannot be rectified remotely, the Contractor shall send a qualified technician to the Customer's plant.

Repairs shall be carried out with the aim of restoring the full functionality of the Equipment. Where a permanent repair is not possible within the restoration time, for example because spare parts must be ordered, the Contractor shall, where technically justifiable, implement a temporary solution that allows the Equipment to continue operating until the permanent repair can be completed. The Contractor shall inform the Customer of any restrictions associated with the temporary solution.
2.3 Spare Parts

The Contractor shall keep a stock of wear and spare parts for the Equipment at its regional service base. The minimum stock is specified in Annex 2 and covers in particular filters, seals, hydraulic hoses, sensors, contactors, cutting nozzles and protective glasses. The Contractor shall review the minimum stock annually with the Customer and adjust it to the actual consumption.

Spare parts shall be original parts of the respective Equipment manufacturer or parts of equivalent quality. The use of non-original parts requires the prior consent of the Customer in text form for safety-relevant components.

Wear parts consumed during preventive maintenance are included in the flat fee pursuant to clause 5.1, up to a value of EUR 2,500 per calendar quarter. Spare parts for corrective maintenance and wear parts exceeding this value shall be invoiced separately at the Contractor's list prices less a discount of 12 percent.
2.4 Occupational Safety on Site

The Contractor's technicians shall comply with the Customer's plant regulations and safety rules set out in Annex 4. Before starting any work, the technician shall register with the shift supervisor and agree on the release of the Equipment. Work on Equipment may only begin after the Equipment has been shut down and secured against restarting in accordance with the Customer's lockout procedure. Each technician shall use a personal padlock and shall remove it personally after completing the work.

The Contractor shall provide its technicians with the personal protective equipment required for the respective work, including safety shoes, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection and, for work on the laser cutting systems, laser protection goggles. Hot work, such as welding or grinding outside the designated areas, requires a written permit from the Customer's fire safety officer.

The Contractor shall report any accident or near miss involving its technicians on the Customer's premises to the Customer's occupational safety specialist on the same day. The Parties shall analyse such events jointly and agree on measures to prevent recurrence.
3. Response Times and Service Levels

The Contractor guarantees the following response times and restoration targets, depending on the priority of the malfunction. The response time begins upon receipt of the fault report by the Contractor and ends when a qualified technician begins troubleshooting, either remotely or on site. The priority is determined by the Customer when reporting the fault; the Contractor may propose a different classification, but may not delay its response for this reason.
Priority
Definition
Response time
Restoration target
Priority 1 – Critical
Production standstill of a bottleneck machine or a safety risk
2 hours, 24/7
8 hours
Priority 2 – High
Equipment failure with significant production impact, alternative capacity available
4 hours during service hours
24 hours
Priority 3 – Medium
Restricted operation, quality or performance impaired
Next working day
3 working days
Priority 4 – Low
Minor defects without impact on production
5 working days
Next scheduled maintenance

The service hours of the Contractor are Monday to Friday from 6:00 to 22:00 and Saturday from 6:00 to 14:00. For Priority 1 malfunctions, the Contractor shall operate an on-call service outside these hours, including Sundays and public holidays.

The Contractor shall achieve an availability of at least 97 percent for the bottleneck machines designated in Annex 1, measured over a calendar quarter in relation to the Customer's planned production time. Downtimes caused by preventive maintenance agreed with the Customer, by the Customer's own fault or by force majeure are not taken into account.

If the Contractor fails to meet the response time for a Priority 1 malfunction, the Customer shall be entitled to a contractual penalty of EUR 500 for each hour or part thereof of delay, up to a maximum of EUR 5,000 per incident. If the availability target is not achieved in a calendar quarter, the flat fee for that quarter shall be reduced by 5 percent for each full percentage point below the target, up to a maximum of 20 percent. Further claims for damages remain unaffected, but contractual penalties shall be offset against them.

The Contractor shall provide the Customer with a quarterly service report containing the number of fault reports by priority, the actual response and restoration times, the availability of the bottleneck machines and recommendations for improving the reliability of the Equipment. The Parties shall discuss the report in a quarterly review meeting.
If a Priority 1 or Priority 2 malfunction cannot be rectified within the restoration target, the following escalation levels apply:
Level 1:
the service technician on site informs the Contractor's service manager and the Customer's maintenance manager, stating the cause and the expected repair time.
Level 2:

if the restoration target is exceeded by more than 50 percent, the Contractor's service manager and the Customer's plant manager agree on further measures, such as the involvement of the Equipment manufacturer or the provision of replacement capacity.
Level 3:
if the malfunction persists for more than 72 hours, the managing directors of both Parties are informed and decide on the further course of action.
4. Obligations of the Customer
To enable the Contractor to perform its services properly, the Customer shall:
grant the Contractor's technicians access to the Equipment during the agreed times and, for Priority 1 malfunctions, at any time
name a responsible contact person for each shift, who is authorised to release Equipment for maintenance work
provide the technical documentation of the Equipment, including operating instructions, circuit diagrams and maintenance records, insofar as it is available to the Customer
instruct the Contractor's technicians in the plant regulations, the safety rules and the emergency procedures before their first assignment
provide electricity, compressed air, lifting equipment and a lockable storage space for tools and spare parts free of charge
operate the Equipment in accordance with the manufacturers' instructions and have daily checks carried out by trained operators
report malfunctions without undue delay and provide all information necessary for diagnosis
inform the Contractor in good time of planned changes to the Equipment, its location or its operating conditions

If the Customer fails to fulfil these obligations and this delays the Contractor's services, the agreed response and restoration times shall be extended accordingly. Additional expenses incurred by the Contractor as a result may be invoiced at the hourly rates in Annex 3.
5. Remuneration and Payment Terms

5.1 For preventive maintenance in accordance with clause 2.1, the Customer shall pay the Contractor a monthly flat fee of EUR 14,850 plus statutory VAT. The flat fee covers all labour and travel costs for preventive maintenance as well as wear parts up to the value specified in clause 2.3.
5.2 Corrective maintenance shall be invoiced according to actual time spent at the following hourly rates, plus statutory VAT:
service technician, Monday to Friday 6:00 to 22:00: EUR 98 per hour
service technician, Saturday and outside service hours: EUR 137 per hour
service technician, Sundays and public holidays: EUR 176 per hour
specialist for control technology and robotics: plus EUR 22 per hour on the respective rate
Travel time is invoiced as a flat rate of EUR 85 per assignment. No travel costs shall be charged for assignments carried out on the same day as a scheduled maintenance visit.

5.3 The Contractor shall invoice the flat fee monthly in advance and the services for corrective maintenance monthly in arrears. Each invoice for corrective maintenance shall be accompanied by the corresponding service reports. Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt without deduction, or within 14 days with a 2 percent discount.

5.4 The prices are fixed until 31 December 2027. Thereafter, the Contractor may adjust the flat fee and the hourly rates once per calendar year with effect from 1 January, in line with the change in the index of collectively agreed wages in the metal and electrical industry, by giving notice in text form by 30 September of the previous year. If the increase exceeds 5 percent, the Customer may terminate the contract with effect from the date of the price adjustment.
6. Liability and Warranty

6.1 The Contractor warrants that repairs and replaced parts are free from defects for a period of twelve months from completion of the respective repair. In the event of a defect, the Contractor shall at its own discretion rectify the defect or carry out the repair again. If the subsequent performance fails twice, the Customer may reduce the remuneration for the repair concerned or withdraw from the individual order.

6.2 The Contractor shall be liable without limitation for damage resulting from injury to life, body or health and for damage caused intentionally or through gross negligence. The same applies to claims under the Product Liability Act and in the case of a guarantee expressly assumed.

6.3 In the event of a slightly negligent breach of an essential contractual obligation, the liability of the Contractor shall be limited to the foreseeable damage typical for this type of contract. Essential contractual obligations are those whose fulfilment makes the proper performance of the contract possible in the first place and on whose observance the Customer may regularly rely. Liability for loss of production and lost profit in such cases shall be limited to EUR 250,000 per incident and EUR 500,000 per contract year.

6.4 The Contractor shall maintain business liability insurance with a coverage of at least EUR 5 million for personal injury and property damage and EUR 1 million for financial loss, and shall provide evidence of this insurance to the Customer upon request.
7. Confidentiality and Data Protection

7.1 The Parties shall treat as confidential all information about the other Party's business that becomes known to them in connection with this contract, in particular technical documentation, production data, prices and customer relationships. This obligation continues for five years after the end of the contract. The Contractor shall impose the same obligation on its employees and any subcontractors.

7.2 Insofar as the Contractor processes personal data on behalf of the Customer in the course of remote diagnosis or when accessing machine controls, the Parties shall conclude a separate data processing agreement in accordance with Article 28 GDPR before such access takes place.

7.3 The Contractor may only establish remote access to the Equipment via the remote maintenance platform provided by the Customer. Each remote session must be requested in advance and approved by the Customer's shift supervisor. The Contractor shall comply with the Customer's IT security requirements, which are available on the
supplier information page
8. Subcontractors

The Contractor may use subcontractors for the performance of individual services, in particular for statutory inspections of cranes and industrial trucks, provided that the subcontractors have the necessary qualifications and certifications. The use of subcontractors for corrective maintenance on bottleneck machines requires the prior consent of the Customer in text form. The Contractor shall be liable for the fault of its subcontractors as for its own fault.
9. Term and Termination

9.1 This contract shall enter into force on [DATE_1] and is concluded for an initial term of three years. Thereafter, it shall be extended automatically by one year at a time unless terminated by either Party with six months' notice to the end of the respective term.
9.2 The right of either Party to terminate the contract for good cause remains unaffected. Good cause for the Customer exists in particular if:
the Contractor fails to meet the response time for Priority 1 malfunctions more than three times within a calendar quarter
the availability target pursuant to clause 3 is missed in two consecutive quarters
the Contractor seriously violates occupational safety regulations or the Customer's plant regulations despite a written warning
insolvency proceedings are opened against the assets of the other Party or the opening of such proceedings is rejected for lack of assets

9.3 Termination must be made in writing. Upon termination of the contract, the Contractor shall hand over all service reports, measurement records and documentation relating to the Equipment to the Customer and shall support the transfer of maintenance to a successor for a period of up to three months against payment at the agreed hourly rates.
10. Final Provisions

10.1 Amendments and supplements to this contract must be made in text form. This also applies to any waiver of the text form requirement. The general terms and conditions of the Contractor shall not apply, even if the Customer does not expressly object to them. The Customer's general purchasing conditions, available at
example.com/terms/purchasing
, apply in addition insofar as this contract does not contain any deviating provisions.

10.2 Should any provision of this contract be or become invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions shall not be affected. The Parties shall replace the invalid provision with a valid provision that comes as close as possible to the economic purpose of the invalid provision.

10.3 This contract is governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. The exclusive place of jurisdiction for all disputes arising from or in connection with this contract is the registered office of the Customer.
10.4 The following annexes form an integral part of this contract:
Annex 1: List of Equipment, including the designation of bottleneck machines
Annex 2: Minimum stock of spare and wear parts
Annex 3: Price list for additional services
Annex 4: Plant regulations and safety rules of the Customer
Signatures
For the Customer: [PERSON_1], Managing Director, [ORG_1]. Place and date: [LOCATION_1], [DATE_2].
For the Contractor: [PERSON_2], Managing Director, [ORG_2]. Place and date: [LOCATION_2], [DATE_3].
